title: service-storage: decide who owns `sys_file`'s reference columns (`ref_*`, `released_ref_*`), which stay writable through the data door after #27399

Found by the dev of #27399 (PR #27765, os-dev-report `6510110320`, out-of-scope findings). Read from the code only; no door was measured. Out of that card's scope.

## What may be wrong

#27765 makes the five columns of `sys_file` that the storage service owns (`key`, `mime_type`, `size`, `status`, `etag`) unwritable outside the storage service. The reference columns that record which record and field a file belongs to (`ref_object`, `ref_id`, `ref_field`) and which one released it (`released_ref_object`, `released_ref_id`) are still plain fields. A caller that may write `sys_file` can set them through the data door. The file-reference lifecycle maintains them as the system context, and other code may trust them as the file's ownership.

## Expected

Triage decides whether these columns are owned by the file-reference lifecycle like the five storage columns (`readonly` on the object and the same create-side guard as #27765, no new refusal), and whether anything that trusts them for access needs re-checking. Grading, including whether this is a `security` card, is triage's.

Re-check after #27765 merges.

Filed without `domain:*`; grading is triage's.
